Curve features of the pubertal spurt: peak width and duration

Source: R/curve-velocity.R
wgh_curve_features.Rd

For each child's velocity curve, finds the times at which velocity crosses given levels on either side of the peak and reports the width between them as a duration of the spurt (Ho 2026, medRxiv 2026.09.09.26362696).

Usage

wgh_curve_features(
  panel,
  thresholds = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75),
  reference = c("takeoff", "zero")
)

Arguments

panel

Output of wgh_velocity_panel() (fine grid recommended).

thresholds

Fractions.

reference

"takeoff" or "zero".

Value

A tibble with one row per child: phv, takeoff, peak_time, and for each threshold the left and right crossing, the width and censoring flags, plus degenerate.

Details

With reference = "takeoff" (default) the levels are fractions of the spurt amplitude above the take-off velocity (the lowest velocity before the peak): level = takeoff + fraction x (PHV - takeoff). With reference = "zero" the levels are fractions of PHV itself, as in the original code of the spurt duration study (Ho 2026, medRxiv 2026.09.09.26362696). Because prepubertal velocity is often above half of PHV, the fraction-of-PHV definition frequently has no left crossing and the duration degenerates to a censored value for most children. Crossings that fall outside the curve are reported as censored, and curves whose peak is at the edge of the grid are flagged as degenerate.

Examples

# \donttest{
boys <- growdat2_mini[growdat2_mini$sex == "Male", ]
fit <- wgh_fit_sitar(boys, df = 4, age_range = c(6, 18))
pan <- wgh_velocity_panel(fit, time = "aphv", grid = seq(-4, 4, by = 0.05), observed_only = FALSE)
cf <- wgh_curve_features(pan)
summary(cf$width_p50)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   1.977   2.182   2.258   2.266   2.343   2.763 
# The legacy definition (fraction of peak velocity) is often censored
mean(wgh_curve_features(pan, thresholds = 0.5, reference = "zero")$censored_left_p50)
#> [1] 1
# }
